"Create a fully playable 3D cartoon-style obstacle-course competition game inspired by the classic Wipeout TV show and console games.

CORE GAMEPLAY:
Build a round-based obstacle-course competition where the player controls a character and must survive increasingly difficult obstacle courses. The competition must progress through multiple rounds, with the final round always called WIPEOUT ZONE. Players must physically control their characters throughout the entire game. The game must NEVER play itself.

ROUND STRUCTURE:

1. Qualifier – Big Red Balls, balance beams, slippery platforms and moving obstacles.
2. Sweeper Challenge – rotating sweepers, jumping platforms and moving hazards.
3. Dizzy Zone – spinning platforms, swinging obstacles and difficult balance challenges.
4. WIPEOUT ZONE – a massive final obstacle course combining multiple obstacle types, difficult jumps, moving hazards and a final finish platform.

Include qualification systems, elimination, checkpoints, timers, leaderboards and results screens.

CHARACTER SELECTION:
Create at least 20 different selectable cartoon characters with different body shapes, heights, weights and physical attributes. Include tall skinny characters, short chunky characters, heavy characters, muscular characters, athletic characters and lightweight characters.

Each character must have individual stats for speed, jumping, balance, strength, stamina and recovery. These stats must genuinely affect gameplay. Characters must have unique appearances, animations and personalities. Include unlockable characters and character customisation.

OBSTACLE LIBRARY:
Include giant Big Red Balls, rotating sweeper arms, swinging hammers, surprise punching obstacles, slippery ramps, collapsing platforms, moving walls, rotating cylinders, balance beams, launch pads and other creative obstacle challenges.

Obstacles must have functional physics and proper collision detection.

PHYSICS AND ANIMATIONS:
Implement funny, exaggerated ragdoll physics. Characters must stumble, fall, bounce, slide, tumble, get knocked backwards and fly into the water. Include recovery animations when getting back up. Falling into water must trigger proper splash effects and a respawn or checkpoint system.

ARENAS:
Create multiple visually distinct 3D competition environments, including Classic Wipeout Arena, Tropical Island, Winter Wipeout, Desert Arena, Nighttime Stadium and Extreme Industrial Arena. Each arena must have unique scenery, obstacle arrangements and visual effects.

GAME MODES:
Include Career Mode, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial and Endless Wipeout. Build progression with unlockable characters, costumes, celebrations and rewards.

VISUAL STYLE:
Use colourful, exaggerated, polished 3D cartoon graphics. Characters, obstacles, arenas, water, scenery and menus should have proper 3D models. Avoid realistic graphics and avoid making the game look like a 2D mobile game.

CAMERA AND CONTROLS:
Use a third-person camera that follows the player's character closely while keeping upcoming obstacles visible. Include responsive mobile touchscreen controls for movement, jumping, sprinting and diving. Controls must be comfortable on mobile devices.

IMPORTANT:
Prioritise actual playable gameplay over menus and decorative features. Build fully functional courses, working obstacles, character physics, collision detection, round progression and a proper Wipeout Zone finale. Do not create fake buttons, placeholder obstacles or automated gameplay. Optimise performance for mobile devices.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

Architecture:
- Vite vanilla JS + three

- ui.js menus (DOM overlays) with character select, mode select, results, leaderboard

I'll implement: W/S forward/back, A/D strafe (camera-relative), Space jump, Shift sprint, X/C dive. Mobile: virtual joystick left, jump/sprint/dive buttons right. Camera follows behind player with yaw fixed toward course direction, staying 8-10 units back, 4.5 up, with lookahead.

Physics: player as a sphere/capsule on top of platforms; gravity, ground detection via ray against platform list; obstacles collision:
- Balls: sphere-push, big red balls rolling/bouncing; if touched while on platform, knock player.
- Sweeper arms: rotating horizontal beams, box collision -> knockback + tumble.

Player states: run, jump, stumble, knocked (ragdoll spin), falling, splash, recover, finished. Lives / respawn at checkpoint after splash with penalty.

Round structure: 4 rounds; fail => eliminated unless qualification? Include qualifier system: need to finish within time / among AI rivals? Add AI rivals as simple bots that follow course and can be knocked. Leaderboard ranks player vs bots. Elimination: if player splashes too many times (e.g. 3) or time expires, eliminated. To keep it fun, generous.

Course generation: procedurally constructed per round & arena with deterministic seed, themed visuals. Each round has segments with obstacles. Arena variants choose backdrop theme.

Round 1 qualifier: big balls, beams, slippery, moving obstacles.
Round 2 sweeper: rotating sweepers, jump platforms, moving hazards.
Round 3 dizzy: spinning platforms, swinging hammers, balance.
Round 4 Wipeout Zone: all combined, gaps, finish.

Settings include difficulty.

Let me design gameplay concretely to ensure it works.

Coordinate system: Course runs along -Z from start z=0 to finish z=-length. Player starts at z=2 facing -Z. Platforms segments defined as boxes with top y level (mostly 0). Water at y=-3.5. Platforms have center (x,z), size (w,d), top Y. Gaps between segments create jumping challenges. Checkpoints at z positions where respawn.

Course layout: total length maybe 220-320 units for round 4. Segment sequence with width 14 (arena). Player movement speed ~ 9 units/s base with stats speed factor 0.85-1.25 and sprint 1.5. Round lasts 60-120 sec.

Build course from "sections", each section ~24-40 units deep:
- flat platform with obstacles
- ball section: red balls rolling toward player (spawn periodically at far end, roll +Z), placed across path
- sweeper section: rotating arm around center pivot at platform level, arm length 8, rotates horizontally at ~1 rev/3s; must jump or duck? Jump over arm — arm lower, jump clears.
- beam section: narrow beam width 2.2 over water with swinging hammers
- slippery ramp: tilted platform with low friction, sliding sideways? keep simple: sloped platform, friction low so acceleration slides; plus push walls.
- collapsing platforms: tiles that disappear in sequence, need run through quickly.
- punching gloves: box glove pulses out from side at intervals.
- moving walls: barriers oscillating across the path.
- rotating cylinders: horizontal cylinder rotating about Z? Roll across width; collision pushes.
- launch pad: pad that launches player forward/up big.
- gap jumps: platform gaps requiring jump.
- finish platform wide with banner.

Collision design:
Player capsule approximated by sphere at feet center (radius 0.45, height 1.7). Ground: determine platform under player via AABB XZ and top Y near feet within step threshold. Use "highest platform top <= feetY + 0.35 and > water" pick. For airborne, land when falling and feetY <= top and previous feetY >= top-0.2. Simpler: feet Y, groundY = max top among platforms containing XZ (and top <= feetY + 0.5). Apply gravity; if feetY < groundY: snap, grounded. If no platform: fall to water -> splash.

Platform edges: walking off edge -> fall. Good.

Slopes: implement ramps as platform with topY varying along z (height function) for visual slide. Might skip slopes for collision simplicity but need slippery ramps. Could model "slippery" as low friction zone, with slight incline visual? We can implement tilted quads as top plane; ground height computed by plane equation. Add `slope` property {dir, amount} topY = baseY + amount * (position along dir normalized). Then physics slides. Hmm adds complexity but doable: groundAt(x,z) computes top for each platform where within bounds, including slope. Landing/ground snap works. Movement friction reduced in slippery zone via platform.slippery.

For platform gaps: course builder creates segments with gaps of 3-4 units; jumping distance at speed 9, jump vy=8, gravity 26 → airtime ~0.61s*9≈5.5 units. Fine.

Obstacle collisions: each obstacle gives colliders:
- sphere {type:'sphere', pos, r, vx,vz}
- box oriented around Y (sweeper arm): use closest point in local space; treat as capsule/cylinder horizontal at height. Compute player distance to rotating box; if within, apply knock.
- hammer: box at end.
Knock response: character enters 'tumble' state with random angular velocity, velocity impulse away, control reduced for ~1.1s, then recover at current spot if grounded. Hitting water while tumbling -> splash.

Ragdoll visual: character mesh group rotates (tumble) with limbs splayed; use procedural animation. Full ragdoll overkill. Use "cartoon ragdoll" tumble of the whole body + limbs flail. Good.

Splash: water particle burst, ring, camera shake, audio; respawn at last checkpoint after 1.4s with countdown and penalty +3s; splash count++. If splashes >= 3 => eliminated (results screen). Checkpoint pass increases respawn.

Timer: round time; HUD shows time, splashes, position, progress bar.

Qualification/elimination: need to finish. AI rivals times: assign target pace/arrival times; leaderboard at end with rank. If player eliminated, results screen "ELIMINATED" — but in career, should retry option. Include "Qualification" round: must finish top 6 of 8; since AI times fixed, player just needs finish before X time. Show qualifiers. Keep player's rank computed by progress among bots live.

Rounds progression: Career runs 4 rounds; each completion unlocks next round & rewards. If fail, retry round (no progress, maybe lose run). Championship: 4 rounds (each arena rotation, harder AI), points. Quick Play: single selected round. Time Trial: race clock, no eliminations, best time per course saved. Endless: start round 1 scenery, procedurally generated rounds with increasing speed until 3 splashes; leaderboard longest distance/rounds.

Character stats genuinely affect:
- speed: move speed, sprint
- jump: jump velocity, air control
- balance: recovery time, chance to resist knockback, beam stability (wobble)
- strength: knockback resistance, push obstacles, maybe punch objects away
- stamina: sprint duration/energy drain
- recovery: get-up time, splash penalty
Height/weight affect body scale, collisions (slightly), inertia and ragdoll.

Camera follows player: position = player pos + offset rotated by camera yaw. Auto-align yaw toward course (-Z) slowly, allow right-drag / touch drag to orbit? Sprint: stamina meter drains, speed boost 1.45x; regen when idle.

Balancing aspects: balance stat affects resistance to tangential drift and wobble (visual lean), and tumble.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D cartoon obstacle-course competition game inspired by Wipeout, including rounds, characters, obstacles, arenas, progression, and mobile controls.

## Requirements
- Fully playable third-person gameplay; no automated player control.
- Four-round structure ending with a course always named WIPEOUT ZONE.
- 20+ selectable characters with meaningful physical-stat differences, unlocks, and customization.
- Functional physics, obstacles, splashes, respawns, checkpoints, timers, leaderboards, elimination/result screens, and ragdoll-like movement.
- Career, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial, and Endless modes.
- Multiple themed 3D arenas and mobile-optimized controls.

## Decisions
- Use Vite, Three.js, procedural 3D geometry, and WebAudio.
- Keep the game asset-light with generated characters, arenas, and effects.
- Implement characters and opponents as real rigs; opponents act as competitors rather than controlling the player.
- Use localStorage for progression and leaderboards.

## Work State
### Completed
- Scaffolded Vite/Three.js project and build scripts.
- Created 24-character roster with stats, unlock requirements, body variants, outfits, personalities, and procedural rigs.
- Implemented character physics metrics for speed, jump, balance, strength, stamina, recovery, knock resistance, and grip.
- Implemented obstacle classes for balls, sweepers, hammers, punches, ramps, platforms, walls, rollers, launch pads, and checkpoints.
- Implemented four course round types and six arena themes.
- Implemented environment, water, scenery, crowd, weather, and visual animation systems.
- Implemented player movement, jumping, diving, stamina, knockback, tumbling, splash respawns, and recovery.
- Implemented bot competitors, race positions, and championship planning.
- Implemented menus, roster, setup, HUD, results, standings, pause, touch controls, keyboard input, and local leaderboards.
- Implemented career/save/costume/token/character progression and audio synthesis.
- Started a local development server and performed browser smoke testing.
- Found and fixed a missing course-to-game-scene attachment bug.

### Active
- Final browser gameplay validation and visual tuning.

### Blocked
- No remaining technical blocker is recorded.
- Full end-to-end course completion and final visual polish still need verification.

## Next Move
1. Run `npm run build` and resolve any bundler errors.
2. Test Qualifier through WIPEOUT ZONE end-to-end in browser.
3. Verify checkpoints, splash respawns, finish ranking, results, unlocks, and round progression.
4. Recheck desktop and mobile camera framing and touch controls.
5. Save and inspect a final small JPEG smoke-test screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: Main game orchestration, modes, camera, race state, and course lifecycle.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/player.js`: Player movement, physics, stamina, obstacles, splashes, and recovery.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/course.js`: Round layouts, platforms, checkpoints, finish, and course construction.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/obstacles.js`: Obstacle collision and animation library.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/characters.js`: 24-character roster and gameplay-stat derivation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/characterRig.js`: Procedural cartoon character meshes and animations.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: Arenas, water, scenery, atmosphere, and environmental effects.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/themes.js`: Arena themes, rounds, and game-mode definitions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js`: Menus, roster, setup, HUD, results, standings, and touch UI.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/bots.js`: AI competitor timing and ranking.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/save.js`: Local progression and leaderboard persistence.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/input.js`: Keyboard and touchscreen controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/style.css`: Full responsive visual styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: App shell and UI structure.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/package.json`: Scripts and dependencies.

## Important Context
- Development server command: `npm run dev -- --port 3002`.
- Build command: `npm run build`.
- Game is exposed for browser automation at `window.__wipeout = { game, ui, save, input, audio, renderer, THREE }`.
- The course bug fixed by adding `course.group` to `scene`.
- The game uses a start-position and direction convention where forward/negative-Z progression is important.

"Create a fully playable 3D cartoon-style obstacle-course competition game inspired by the classic Wipeout TV show and console games.

CORE GAMEPLAY:
Build a round-based obstacle-course competition where the player controls a character and must survive increasingly difficult obstacle courses. The competition must progress through multiple rounds, with the final round always called WIPEOUT ZONE. Players must physically control their characters throughout the entire game. The game must NEVER play itself.

ROUND STRUCTURE:

1. Qualifier – Big Red Balls, balance beams, slippery platforms and moving obstacles.
2. Sweeper Challenge – rotating sweepers, jumping platforms and moving hazards.
3. Dizzy Zone – spinning platforms, swinging obstacles and difficult balance challenges.
4. WIPEOUT ZONE – a massive final obstacle course combining multiple obstacle types, difficult jumps, moving hazards and a final finish platform.

Include qualification systems, elimination, checkpoints, timers, leaderboards and results screens.

CHARACTER SELECTION:
Create at least 20 different selectable cartoon characters with different body shapes, heights, weights and physical attributes. Include tall skinny characters, short chunky characters, heavy characters, muscular characters, athletic characters and lightweight characters.

Each character must have individual stats for speed, jumping, balance, strength, stamina and recovery. These stats must genuinely affect gameplay. Characters must have unique appearances, animations and personalities. Include unlockable characters and character customisation.

OBSTACLE LIBRARY:
Include giant Big Red Balls, rotating sweeper arms, swinging hammers, surprise punching obstacles, slippery ramps, collapsing platforms, moving walls, rotating cylinders, balance beams, launch pads and other creative obstacle challenges.

Obstacles must have functional physics and proper collision detection.

PHYSICS AND ANIMATIONS:
Implement funny, exaggerated ragdoll physics. Characters must stumble, fall, bounce, slide, tumble, get knocked backwards and fly into the water. Include recovery animations when getting back up. Falling into water must trigger proper splash effects and a respawn or checkpoint system.

ARENAS:
Create multiple visually distinct 3D competition environments, including Classic Wipeout Arena, Tropical Island, Winter Wipeout, Desert Arena, Nighttime Stadium and Extreme Industrial Arena. Each arena must have unique scenery, obstacle arrangements and visual effects.

GAME MODES:
Include Career Mode, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial and Endless Wipeout. Build progression with unlockable characters, costumes, celebrations and rewards.

VISUAL STYLE:
Use colourful, exaggerated, polished 3D cartoon graphics. Characters, obstacles, arenas, water, scenery and menus should have proper 3D models. Avoid realistic graphics and avoid making the game look like a 2D mobile game.

CAMERA AND CONTROLS:
Use a third-person camera that follows the player's character closely while keeping upcoming obstacles visible. Include responsive mobile touchscreen controls for movement, jumping, sprinting and diving. Controls must be comfortable on mobile devices.

IMPORTANT:
Prioritise actual playable gameplay over menus and decorative features. Build fully functional courses, working obstacles, character physics, collision detection, round progression and a proper Wipeout Zone finale. Do not create fake buttons, placeholder obstacles or automated gameplay. Optimise performance for mobile devices.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and finalize a complete, playable 3D cartoon obstacle-course competition game inspired by Wipeout.

## Requirements
- Provide fully manual third-person gameplay across four rounds, with WIPEOUT ZONE always as round four.
- Include 20+ customizable characters, unlock progression, six arenas, career and alternate modes, physics, obstacles, checkpoints, leaderboards, results, and elimination.
- Support responsive keyboard and mobile touch controls with no automated player control.
- Prioritize playable courses and end-to-end round progression over decoration.

## Decisions
- Use Vite, Three.js, procedural geometry, and WebAudio.
- Use asset-light generated characters and environments.
- Persist progression and leaderboards in localStorage.
- Implement competitors as real bot rigs and never substitute them for player control.
- Forward movement progresses toward negative Z.

## Work State
### Completed
- Scaffolded Vite/Three.js project and production build scripts.
- Added 24-character roster, character stats, unlocks, body variants, costumes, and procedural rigs.
- Implemented movement, stamina, jumping, diving, knocks, tumbling, splashes, respawns, and checkpoints.
- Implemented obstacle, arena, course, bot, HUD, menu, results, progression, and audio systems.
- Added Career, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial, and Endless modes.
- Added course attachment, ensuring `course.group` is part of the game scene.
- Verified `npm run build` passes successfully.
- Ran browser smoke tests for title, setup, countdown, racing, splashes, results, and mobile framing.
- Confirmed checkpoint and finish state transitions through automated position testing.
- Captured and inspected desktop and mobile screenshots.

### Active
- Final browser gameplay validation and visual tuning remain to be completed.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Complete a full uninterrupted player-controlled Qualifier-to-WIPEOUT-ZONE run.
2. Verify obstacle hits, all checkpoint respawns, qualification thresholds, round advancement, eliminations, finish ranking, unlocks, and leaderboard persistence.
3. Recheck desktop and mobile camera framing, touch controls, performance, and visual polish.
4. Save one final small JPEG viewport screenshot and inspect it.
5. Run a final production build after any tuning changes.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: Main race orchestration, modes, camera, state, and round lifecycle.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/player.js`: Manual movement, physics, collision response, stamina, and respawns.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/course.js`: Round layouts, platforms, checkpoints, finish, and course construction.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/obstacles.js`: Big Balls, sweepers, hammers, punches, ramps, walls, rollers, and launch pads.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/characters.js`: 24-character roster and gameplay-stat derivation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/characterRig.js`: Procedural character meshes and animation rigs.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: Arenas, water, scenery, crowd, and weather.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/themes.js`: Arena themes, round definitions, and game modes.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js`: Menus, setup, HUD, results, standings, and roster.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/bots.js`: Competitor timing, ranks, and AI race rail.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/save.js`: Progression and local leaderboard persistence.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/input.js`: Keyboard and touchscreen controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/style.css`: Responsive HUD, menus, and touch styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/package.json`: Build and development scripts.

## Important Context
- The game is exposed at `window.__wipeout = { game, ui, save, input, audio, renderer, THREE }`.
- Browser smoke testing confirmed Qualifier can enter racing, fall for splash respawns, reach results, and complete finish-state transitions.
- Automated testing reached results for a teleported Time Trial run with rank 1 and `state: "results"`.
- The development server was last observed on port 3002, with an additional Vite instance on port 3003.
- Runtime build output is in `dist/`; source and project state remain uncommitted as untracked files.

## Objective
- Complete and finalize a playable 3D cartoon obstacle-course competition game inspired by Wipeout, with fully manual gameplay and a four-round finale named WIPEOUT ZONE.

## Requirements
- Support Career, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial, and Endless modes; character customization and unlocks; six arenas; obstacles, physics, checkpoints, leaderboards, results, and eliminations.
- Use responsive keyboard and mobile touch controls; never automate player control.
- Prioritize playable courses and round progression over decoration.

## Decisions
- Use Vite, Three.js, procedural geometry, and WebAudio.
- Persist progression and leaderboards in localStorage; implement competitors as separate bot rigs.
- Forward movement progresses toward negative Z.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game systems, including 24 characters, multiple modes and arenas, obstacle courses, physics, progression, menus, HUD, and persistence.
- Verified `npm run build` passes and smoke-tested title, setup, countdown, racing, splashes, results, finish-state transitions, and mobile framing.
- Verified checkpoint and finish transitions with automated position testing.

### Active
- Final browser gameplay validation and visual tuning.
- A manually controlled Career run ended in elimination after three splashes; an attempted forward-plus-strafe input moved the player off the course.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue manual gameplay testing with centered forward input and deliberate steering; verify checkpoint respawns and round advancement through WIPEOUT ZONE.
2. Check qualification/elimination, finish ranking, unlocks, and leaderboard persistence.
3. Recheck desktop/mobile framing, touch controls, performance, and visual polish; save and inspect a final small JPEG screenshot.
4. Run `npm run build` after any changes.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: Race orchestration, round lifecycle, camera, and modes.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/player.js`: Manual movement, physics, collisions, and respawns.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/course.js`: Course layouts, platforms, checkpoints, and finish.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/obstacles.js`: Obstacle behavior and collision logic.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/input.js`: Keyboard and touchscreen controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js`: Menus, HUD, standings, and results.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/save.js`: Progression and leaderboard persistence.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/style.css`: Responsive styling and touch controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/package.json`: Build and development scripts.

## Important Context
- `window.__wipeout = { game, ui, save, input, audio, renderer, THREE }` exposes runtime state for browser validation.
- Browser smoke tests observed zero console errors and five warnings; production build had passed previously.
- The Career run started at `[0,0,8]` but after holding `w` and `d` reached `[11.10,-8.57,-0.10]`, took three splashes, and was eliminated. Further validation should avoid excessive strafe and inspect player movement/collision behavior.
- Repository files were untracked at last status check; no commit was made.

## Objective
- Finalize a playable 3D cartoon obstacle-course competition game inspired by Wipeout, with manual gameplay and a four-round finale named WIPEOUT ZONE.

## Requirements
- Support Career, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial, and Endless modes; character customization and unlocks; six arenas; obstacles, physics, checkpoints, leaderboards, results, and eliminations.
- Provide responsive keyboard and mobile touch controls; never automate player control.
- Prioritize playable courses and round progression over decoration.

## Decisions
- Use Vite, Three.js, procedural geometry, and WebAudio.
- Persist progression and leaderboards in localStorage; implement competitors as separate bot rigs.
- Forward movement progresses toward negative Z.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game systems, including modes, arenas, courses, obstacles, physics, progression, menus, HUD, and persistence.
- Fixed the opening platform gap in `src/course.js`: the first generated section now connects to the start platform.
- Confirmed centered forward movement stays grounded and splash-free through the opening section in a manual browser test.
- `npm run build` passes; smoke-tested menus.

### Active
- Continue manual validation of course continuity, checkpoint respawns, qualification/elimination, round advancement through WIPEOUT ZONE, results, unlocks, and leaderboard persistence.
- Recheck desktop/mobile framing, touch controls, performance, and visual polish; capture and inspect a final small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- A test command failed because `playwright-cli` did not recognize `"shift"` as a key; sprint testing remains pending.

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing with supported keyboard controls, especially sprint, hazards, checkpoints, and full round progression.
2. Validate persistence and responsive controls/framing; inspect a final screenshot.
3. Run `npm run build` after any further changes and review the build warning about the 804.49 kB JavaScript chunk.

## Relevant Files
- `src/course.js`: Course generation and the opening-gap fix.
- `src/player.js`: Movement, ground detection, collisions, and respawns.
- `src/game.js`: Race orchestration, round lifecycle, modes, and HUD updates.
- `src/input.js`: Keyboard and touchscreen controls.
- `src/save.js`: Progression and leaderboard persistence.
- `src/style.css`: Responsive styling and touch controls.
- `package.json`: Build and development scripts.

## Important Context
- `window.__wipeout = { game, ui, save, input, audio, renderer, THREE }` exposes runtime state for browser validation.
- The opening platforms now meet at Z = -2; a centered forward-only test reached approximately Z = -10.6, grounded with zero splashes.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finalize a playable 3D cartoon obstacle-course competition game inspired by Wipeout, including a four-round finale named WIPEOUT ZONE.

## Requirements
- Support Career, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial, and Endless modes; character customization and unlocks; six arenas; obstacles, physics, checkpoints, leaderboards, results, and eliminations.
- Provide responsive keyboard and mobile touch controls; never automate player control.
- Prioritize playable courses and round progression over decoration.

## Decisions
- Use Vite, Three.js, procedural geometry, and WebAudio.
- Persist progression and leaderboards in localStorage; implement competitors as separate bot rigs.
- Forward movement progresses toward negative Z.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game systems, including modes, arenas, courses, obstacles, physics, progression, menus, HUD, and persistence.
- Fixed the opening platform gap in `src/course.js`; centered forward movement stays grounded and splash-free through the opening section.
- `npm run build` passes; menus have been smoke-tested.

### Active
- Continue building and manually validate course continuity, checkpoint respawns, qualification/elimination, round advancement through WIPEOUT ZONE, results, unlocks, and leaderboard persistence.
- Recheck desktop/mobile framing, touch controls, performance, and visual polish; capture and inspect a final small JPEG screenshot.
- Test sprint, hazards, and full round progression.

### Blocked
- Sprint testing is pending because `playwright-cli` did not recognize `"shift"` as a key.

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing with supported keyboard controls, especially sprint, hazards, checkpoints, and full round progression.
2. Validate persistence and responsive controls/framing; inspect a final screenshot.
3. Run `npm run build` after further changes and review the 804.49 kB JavaScript chunk warning.

## Relevant Files
- `src/course.js`: Course generation and opening-gap fix.
- `src/player.js`: Movement, ground detection, collisions, and respawns.
- `src/game.js`: Race orchestration, round lifecycle, modes, and HUD updates.
- `src/input.js`: Keyboard and touchscreen controls.
- `src/save.js`: Progression and leaderboard persistence.
- `src/style.css`: Responsive styling and touch controls.
- `package.json`: Build and development scripts.

## Important Context
- `window.__wipeout = { game, ui, save, input, audio, renderer, THREE }` exposes runtime state for browser validation.
- Opening platforms meet at Z = -2; a centered forward-only test reached approximately Z = -10.6, grounded with zero splashes.
- Build output reports a chunk-size warning for the 804.49 kB minified JavaScript bundle.
- Repository files were untracked at last status check; no commit was made.

## Objective
- Finalize a playable 3D cartoon obstacle-course competition game inspired by Wipeout, including the four-round WIPEOUT ZONE finale.

## Requirements
- Support Career, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial, and Endless modes; customization and unlocks; six arenas; obstacles, physics, checkpoints, leaderboards, results, and eliminations.
- Provide responsive keyboard and mobile touch controls; never automate player control.
- Prioritize playable courses and round progression over decoration.

## Decisions
- Use Vite, Three.js, procedural geometry, and WebAudio.
- Persist progression and leaderboards in localStorage; implement competitors as separate bot rigs.
- Forward movement progresses toward negative Z.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented core game systems, menus, arenas, courses, obstacles, physics, progression, HUD, and persistence.
- Fixed the opening platform gap; centered forward-only movement stays grounded and splash-free through the opening.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finalize a playable 3D obstacle-course competition game, then make it substantially harder and more varied.
- The WIPEOUT ZONE finale must always be at night and include the hardest obstacles; add more characters and make them harder to unlock.

## Requirements
- Preserve Career, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial, Endless, customization, progression, six arenas, responsive controls, and player-controlled movement.
- Increase obstacle and enemy difficulty, add distinct obstacle types and level variation, and make WIPEOUT ZONE exceptionally difficult.
- Add characters and raise their unlock requirements.

## Decisions
- Continue with the existing Vite, Three.js, procedural-course, and WebAudio implementation.
- Career currently assigns WIPEOUT ZONE to industrial; its arena selection needs to change or otherwise ensure the finale is always night.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game systems and initial gameplay were implemented; `npm run build` passed in the prior work.
- Inspected course generation, obstacle factory, arena themes, characters, unlock handling, and game round setup to plan the difficulty changes.

### Active
- Implement harder and more varied hazards/courses and more competitive enemies.
- Make WIPEOUT ZONE consistently night-themed and exceptionally difficult.
- Add characters and increase unlock costs or requirements.
- Continue the previously pending validation of round progression, hazards, persistence, touch controls, and visual polish.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement additional obstacle types and difficulty/variation changes in `src/obstacles.js` and `src/course.js`.
2. Adjust WIPEOUT ZONE arena selection and night presentation; increase its hazard density and challenge.
3. Improve bot competitiveness, add characters, and raise unlock requirements while keeping progression attainable.
4. Build and browser-test difficulty, progression, responsive controls, and persistence.

## Relevant Files
- `src/course.js`: Procedural sections, obstacle placement, and round layouts.
- `src/obstacles.js`: Obstacle implementations and factory.
- `src/game.js`: Career plans, difficulty scaling, arena selection, and bot setup.
- `src/bots.js`: Rival behavior and race timing.
- `src/themes.js`: Arena themes and round metadata.
- `src/characters.js`: Character roster, stats, and unlock costs.
- `src/save.js`: Token and unlock persistence.
- `src/ui.js`: Roster and character unlock interface.

## Important Context
- Course forward travel progresses toward negative Z.
- Career plan currently selects `{ round: 'wipeout', arena: 'industrial' }`; six arenas include the dedicated `night` theme.
- Obstacle factory currently supports `ball`, `sweeper`, `hammer`, `punch`, `wall`, `roller`, and `launch`; course generation also includes collapsing tiles and spinning discs.
- `src/characters.js` currently has 24 characters; 10 are free and the remaining token unlocks cost 2–12.
- Existing modifications are uncommitted, including changes in `src/characters.js`, `src/course.js`, `src/game.js`, `src/input.js`, `src/player.js`, and `src/style.css`; generated `dist` assets also changed.

## Objective
- Finalize the playable 3D obstacle-course competition game and make it substantially harder and more varied.
- Ensure the WIPEOUT ZONE finale is always at night and exceptionally challenging; add characters and make them harder to unlock.

## Requirements
- Preserve Career, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial, Endless, customization, progression, six arenas, responsive controls, and player-controlled movement.
- Increase obstacle and enemy difficulty, add distinct obstacle types and level variation, and make WIPEOUT ZONE the hardest course.
- Add characters and raise their unlock requirements.

## Decisions
- Continue with the existing Vite, Three.js, procedural-course, and WebAudio implementation.
- Career and Championship currently assign WIPEOUT ZONE to industrial; use the dedicated `night` arena for the finale.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game systems and initial gameplay were implemented; `npm run build` passed in prior work.
- Inspected course generation, obstacle factory, arena themes, characters, unlock handling, and game round setup.
- Confirmed the obstacle factory supports `ball`, `sweeper`, `hammer`, `punch`, `wall`, `roller`, and `launch`; course generation also includes collapsing tiles and spinning discs.

### Active
- Add obstacle types, difficulty scaling, and course variation.
- Make WIPEOUT ZONE consistently night-themed and exceptionally difficult.
- Improve bot competitiveness, add characters, and raise unlock requirements while keeping progression attainable.
- Validate round progression, hazards, persistence, touch controls, and visual polish.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement obstacle and course difficulty/variation changes in `src/obstacles.js` and `src/course.js`.
2. Change the WIPEOUT ZONE finale arena to `night` and tune its hazard density and challenge.
3. Improve bot competitiveness, add characters, and raise unlock costs or requirements.
4. Build and browser-test difficulty, progression, responsive controls, and persistence.

## Relevant Files
- `src/course.js`: Procedural sections, obstacle placement, and round layouts.
- `src/obstacles.js`: Obstacle implementations and factory.
- `src/game.js`: Career plans, difficulty scaling, arena selection, and bot setup.
- `src/bots.js`: Rival behavior and race timing.
- `src/themes.js`: Arena themes and round metadata.
- `src/characters.js`: Character roster, stats, and unlock costs.
- `src/save.js`: Token and unlock persistence.
- `src/ui.js`: Roster and character unlock interface.

## Important Context
- Course forward travel progresses toward negative Z.
- The six arenas include a dedicated `night` theme; Career and Championship currently set the WIPEOUT ZONE arena to `industrial`.
- `src/characters.js` currently has 24 characters; 10 are free and the remaining token unlocks cost 2–12.
- Existing modifications are uncommitted in `src/characters.js`, `src/course.js`, `src/game.js`, `src/input.js`, `src/player.js`, and `src/style.css`; generated `dist` assets also changed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finalize the playable 3D obstacle-course competition game and make it substantially harder and more varied.
- Make the WIPEOUT ZONE finale always take place at night and be exceptionally challenging; add characters and raise their unlock requirements.

## Requirements
- Preserve Career, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial, Endless, customization, progression, six arenas, responsive controls, and player-controlled movement.
- Increase obstacle and enemy difficulty, add distinct obstacle types and level variation, and make WIPEOUT ZONE the hardest course.
- Keep progression and character unlocks attainable.

## Decisions
- Continue with the existing Vite, Three.js, procedural-course, and WebAudio implementation.
- Use the dedicated `night` arena for WIPEOUT ZONE in Career and Championship.
- The obstacle factory supports `ball`, `sweeper`, `hammer`, `punch`, `wall`, `roller`, and `launch`; course generation also includes collapsing tiles and spinning discs.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game systems and initial gameplay were implemented; `npm run build` passed in prior work.
- Inspected course generation, obstacle implementations, round layouts, arena selection, bots, character roster, and unlock persistence/UI.

### Active
- Increase obstacle and course difficulty and variety in `src/obstacles.js` and `src/course.js`.
- Assign the `night` arena to WIPEOUT ZONE in Career and Championship plans in `src/game.js`.
- Improve bot competitiveness, add characters, and raise unlock requirements while keeping progression attainable.
- Validate gameplay, progression, responsive controls, persistence, and visual polish.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Change the WIPEOUT ZONE arena to `night` in both plans in `src/game.js`.
2. Tune WIPEOUT ZONE hazard density and course difficulty; add obstacle/course variety.
3. Improve bot competitiveness, add characters, and raise character unlock costs or requirements.
4. Run `npm run build` and test gameplay, progression, controls, and persistence.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Career and Championship plans, arena selection, difficulty scaling, and bot setup.
- `src/course.js`: Procedural sections, obstacle placement, and round layouts.
- `src/obstacles.js`: Obstacle implementations and factory.
- `src/bots.js`: Rival pacing and behavior.
- `src/characters.js`: Character roster, stats, and unlock costs.
- `src/save.js`: Token and unlock persistence.
- `src/ui.js`: Roster and character unlock interface.
- `src/themes.js`: Arena themes and round metadata.

## Important Context
- Course travel advances toward negative Z.
- Career and Championship currently assign WIPEOUT ZONE to `industrial`, despite a dedicated `night` arena.
- Bot finish times are synthesized from `course.parTime`; stumbles add time, but bots do not navigate hazards.
- There are currently 24 characters, 10 free; token unlock costs range from 2–12.
- Existing modifications are uncommitted in `src/characters.js`, `src/course.js`, `src/game.js`, `src/input.js`, `src/player.js`, and `src/style.css`; generated `dist` assets also changed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finalize the playable 3D obstacle-course competition game, making courses harder and more varied while preserving existing modes and systems.
- Make WIPEOUT ZONE always take place at night, exceptionally challenging, and supported by additional characters with raised but attainable unlock requirements.

## Requirements
- Preserve Career, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial, Endless, customization, progression, six arenas, responsive controls, and player-controlled movement.
- Increase obstacle and enemy difficulty, add distinct obstacle types and level variation, and make WIPEOUT ZONE the hardest course.
- Keep progression and character unlocks attainable.

## Decisions
- Continue with the existing Vite, Three.js, procedural-course, and WebAudio implementation.
- Use the dedicated `night` arena for WIPEOUT ZONE in Career and Championship.
- The obstacle factory supports `ball`, `sweeper`, `hammer`, `punch`, `wall`, `roller`, and `launch`; course generation also includes collapsing tiles and spinning discs.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game systems and initial gameplay are implemented; `npm run build` passed in prior work.
- Inspected course generation, obstacle implementations, round layouts, arena selection, bots, character roster, and unlock persistence/UI.

### Active
- Increase obstacle and course difficulty and variety in `src/obstacles.js` and `src/course.js`.
- Assign the `night` arena to WIPEOUT ZONE in Career and Championship plans in `src/game.js`.
- Improve bot competitiveness, add characters, and raise character unlock costs or requirements while keeping progression attainable.
- Validate gameplay, progression, responsive controls, persistence, and visual polish.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Change WIPEOUT ZONE from `industrial` to `night` in both plans in `src/game.js`.
2. Tune WIPEOUT ZONE hazard density and course difficulty; add obstacle/course variety.
3. Improve bot competitiveness, add characters, and raise unlock requirements or costs.
4. Run `npm run build` and test gameplay, progression, controls, and persistence.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Career and Championship plans, arena selection, difficulty scaling, and bot setup.
- `src/course.js`: Procedural sections, obstacle placement, and round layouts.
- `src/obstacles.js`: Obstacle implementations and factory.
- `src/bots.js`: Rival pacing and behavior.
- `src/characters.js`: Character roster, stats, and unlock costs.
- `src/save.js`: Token and unlock persistence.
- `src/ui.js`: Roster and character unlock interface.
- `src/themes.js`: Arena themes and round metadata.

## Important Context
- Course travel advances toward negative Z.
- Career and Championship currently assign WIPEOUT ZONE to `industrial`, despite a dedicated `night` arena.
- Bots use synthesized finish times based on `course.parTime`; stumbles add time, but bots do not navigate hazards.
- There are currently 24 characters, 10 free, with token unlock costs ranging from 2–12.
- Existing modifications are uncommitted in `src/characters.js`, `src/course.js`, `src/game.js`, `src/input.js`, `src/player.js`, and `src/style.css`; generated `dist` assets also changed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finalize the playable 3D obstacle-course competition game by increasing course difficulty and variety while preserving existing modes and systems.
- Make WIPEOUT ZONE always take place at night, exceptionally challenging, and supported by additional characters with raised but attainable unlock requirements.

## Requirements
- Preserve Career, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial, Endless, customization, progression, six arenas, responsive controls, and player-controlled movement.
- Increase obstacle and enemy difficulty, add distinct obstacle types and level variation, and make WIPEOUT ZONE the hardest course.
- Keep progression and character unlocks attainable.

## Decisions
- Continue with the existing Vite, Three.js, procedural-course, and WebAudio implementation.
- Use the dedicated `night` arena for WIPEOUT ZONE in Career and Championship.
- The obstacle factory supports `ball`, `sweeper`, `hammer`, `punch`, `wall`, `roller`, and `launch`; course generation also includes collapsing tiles and spinning discs.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game systems and initial gameplay are implemented; `npm run build` passed in prior work.
- Inspected current Career and Championship plans, WIPEOUT ZONE layout, obstacle builders, character roster, bot pacing, and token rewards.

### Active
- Assign the `night` arena to WIPEOUT ZONE in Career and Championship plans in `src/game.js`.
- Tune WIPEOUT ZONE hazard density and course difficulty; add obstacle/course variety.
- Improve bot competitiveness, add characters, and raise character unlock costs or requirements while keeping progression attainable.
- Validate gameplay, progression, responsive controls, persistence, and visual polish.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Change WIPEOUT ZONE from `industrial` to `night` in both plans in `src/game.js`.
2. Increase WIPEOUT ZONE challenge and course variety in `src/course.js` and, as needed, `src/obstacles.js`.
3. Improve bot competitiveness, add characters, and tune unlock requirements and token rewards.
4. Run `npm run build` and test gameplay, progression, controls, and persistence.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Career and Championship plans, difficulty scaling, bot setup, and progression rewards.
- `src/course.js`: Procedural sections, obstacle placement, and round layouts.
- `src/obstacles.js`: Obstacle implementations and factory.
- `src/bots.js`: Rival pacing and behavior.
- `src/characters.js`: Character roster, stats, and unlock costs.
- `src/save.js`: Token and unlock persistence.

## Important Context
- Course travel advances toward negative Z.
- Career and Championship currently assign WIPEOUT ZONE to `industrial`, despite the dedicated `night` arena in `src/themes.js`.
- WIPEOUT ZONE already combines balls, sweepers, rollers, walls, collapsing tiles, punches, spinning discs, hammers, a beam, and a launch pad.
- Bots use synthesized finish times based on `course.parTime`; stumbles add time, but bots do not navigate hazards.
- There are currently 24 characters, 10 free, with token unlock costs ranging from 2–12.
- Existing modifications are uncommitted in `src/characters.js`, `src/course.js`, `src/game.js`, `src/input.js`, `src/player.js`, and `src/style.css`; generated `dist` assets also changed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finalize the 3D obstacle-course competition game, increasing course challenge and variety while preserving progression and all existing modes.

## Requirements
- Preserve Career, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial, Endless, customization, progression, six arenas, responsive controls, and player-controlled movement.
- Make WIPEOUT ZONE take place at night, make it exceptionally challenging, and keep character unlocks attainable.

## Decisions
- WIPEOUT ZONE will use the dedicated `night` arena in Career and Championship.
- Existing course systems remain based on Three.js, procedural generation, and WebAudio.
- Character unlock pricing and bot pacing should be raised/tuned moderately rather than made prohibitive.

## Work State
### Completed
- Confirmed `src/game.js` Career and Championship plans currently assign WIPEOUT ZONE to `industrial`.
- Inspected the WIPEOUT layout, obstacle builders, bot pacing, character roster, and course difficulty scaling.
- No implementation edits have been completed beyond the existing uncommitted game changes described in prior context.

### Active
- Assign WIPEOUT ZONE to `night` in both Career and Championship plans.
- Increase WIPEOUT hazard density and course variety.
- Improve bot competitiveness and tune unlock costs/rewards.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Change both WIPEOUT arena assignments in `src/game.js` to `night`.
2. Add tougher density and variety to the WIPEOUT layout in `src/course.js`.
3. Tune bots in `src/bots.js` and raise character unlock requirements in `src/characters.js`.
4. Run `npm run build` and validate gameplay, progression, controls, persistence, and visuals.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Career/Championship plans, session difficulty, bot setup, progression rewards.
- `src/course.js`: Procedural round layouts and WIPEOUT complexity.
- `src/obstacles.js`: Obstacle behavior and factory.
- `src/bots.js`: Rival finish times and pacing.
- `src/characters.js`: 24-character roster and unlock costs.
- `src/save.js`: Token, unlock, and progression persistence.
- `src/themes.js`: Arena definitions, including `night`.
- `dist/`: Generated build assets that may remain modified.

## Important Context
- Course travel advances toward negative Z.
- Existing uncommitted modifications are present in `src/game.js`, `src/course.js`, `src/characters.js`, `src/input.js`, `src/player.js`, and `src/style.css`.
- Bots are timing-rail competitors and do not physically navigate hazards.
- 24 characters exist, with 10 free and unlock costs currently ranging from 2–12 tokens.
- WIPEOUT ZONE already includes balls, sweepers, rollers, walls, collapsing tiles, punches, spinning discs, hammers, beams, and launch pads.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finalize the 3D obstacle-course game by making WIPEOUT ZONE a challenging night course while preserving existing modes and progression.

## Requirements
- Preserve Career, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial, Endless, customization, progression, six arenas, responsive controls, and player-controlled movement.
- Keep character unlocks attainable while moderately tuning prices and bot pacing.

## Decisions
- WIPEOUT ZONE uses the `night` arena in Career and Championship.
- Keep the existing Three.js course systems and timing-rail bots.

## Work State
### Completed
- Changed WIPEOUT ZONE’s Career and Championship arena assignments to `night` in `src/game.js`.
- Increased WIPEOUT hazard density and added combined hazards plus an extra section/checkpoint in `src/course.js`.
- Tightened bot finish-time range in `src/bots.js`.

### Active
- Review and correct character unlock prices in `src/characters.js`; current prices are uneven after bulk edits, including several characters priced at 13 tokens.
- Build and validate the changes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect and rebalance unlock prices, considering Career milestone unlocks and token rewards.
2. Run `npm run build` and review any errors.
3. Check the final diff, preserving existing user changes; verify course and progression behavior if practical.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Career and Championship plans, token rewards, milestone unlocks.
- `src/course.js`: WIPEOUT layout and obstacle builders.
- `src/bots.js`: Bot finish-time pacing.
- `src/characters.js`: Character unlock costs.
- `src/save.js`: Token and unlock persistence.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted. Existing modifications also include `src/input.js`, `src/player.js`, and `src/style.css`.
- `dist/` has deleted old assets, modified `dist/index.html`, and new generated assets; do not assume these changes are disposable.
- Career awards Pixie, Nina, and Bea at milestones and Maxine/Pete for completing the finale; Championship rewards also grant unlocks.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finalize WIPEOUT ZONE as a challenging night course while preserving existing game modes and progression.

## Requirements
- Preserve Career, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial, Endless, customization, progression, six arenas, responsive controls, and player-controlled movement.
- Keep character unlocks attainable while moderately tuning prices and bot pacing.

## Decisions
- WIPEOUT ZONE uses the `night` arena in Career and Championship.
- Keep the existing Three.js course systems and timing-rail bots.

## Work State
### Completed
- Assigned WIPEOUT ZONE to the night arena in Career and Championship.
- Increased WIPEOUT hazard density, combined hazards, and added a section/checkpoint.
- Tightened bot finish-time pacing.
- Adjusted several character unlock prices; milestone characters remain unlockable through Career rewards.

### Active
- Finish reviewing the uneven character unlock prices, including remaining 13-token prices.
- Build and validate the changes; inspect the final diff.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect and rebalance unlock prices in `src/characters.js`, accounting for Career milestone unlocks and token rewards.
2. Run `npm run build` and review errors.
3. Review the final diff and validate course/progression behavior if practical.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Career and Championship plans, rewards, and milestone unlocks.
- `src/course.js`: WIPEOUT layout and obstacle builders.
- `src/bots.js`: Bot finish-time pacing.
- `src/characters.js`: Character unlock costs.
- `src/save.js`: Token and unlock persistence.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted. Existing modifications also affect `src/input.js`, `src/player.js`, and `src/style.css`; preserve those edits.
- `dist/` contains deleted old assets, modified `dist/index.html`, and generated assets; do not assume these changes are disposable.
- Career awards Pixie, Nina, and Bea at milestones and Maxine/Pete for completing the finale; Championship rewards also grant unlocks.
- Current unlock costs are 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6, 6, 13, 13, 13, 13, 13, 15, 15 tokens.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finalize WIPEOUT ZONE as a challenging night course while preserving existing game modes and progression.

## Requirements
- Preserve Career, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial, Endless, customization, progression, six arenas, responsive controls, and player-controlled movement.
- Keep character unlocks attainable while moderately tuning prices and bot pacing.

## Decisions
- WIPEOUT ZONE uses the `night` arena in Career and Championship.
- Keep the existing Three.js course systems and timing-rail bots.

## Work State
### Completed
- Assigned WIPEOUT ZONE to the night arena in Career and Championship.
- Increased WIPEOUT hazard density, combined hazards, and added sections/checkpoints.
- Tightened bot finish-time pacing.
- Rebalanced character prices, including lowering selected 13-token prices; Career milestone and finale unlocks remain intact.
- `npm run build` succeeds; `git diff --check` passes.

### Active
- Review final changes and verify course/progression behavior if practical.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the final diff, including the latest character price adjustment.
2. Validate course and progression behavior if practical.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: Career and Championship plans, rewards, and milestone unlocks.
- `src/course.js`: WIPEOUT layout and obstacle builders.
- `src/bots.js`: Bot finish-time pacing.
- `src/characters.js`: Character unlock costs and physical stats.
- `src/save.js`: Token and unlock persistence.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted. Existing modifications in `src/input.js`, `src/player.js`, and `src/style.css` must be preserved.
- `dist/` had deleted old assets and generated replacements; the latest build generated `dist/assets/index-D1it8Ek5.css` and `dist/assets/index-DcjQS40q.js`. Treat these as existing build-output changes, not disposable.
- Build emits a non-fatal warning that the minified JS chunk is over 500 kB.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the game’s graphics style, enemy AI movement and competition, and obstacle variety.
- Preserve and validate seeded course variation and bot navigation improvements already in progress.

## Requirements
- Preserve existing game modes, customization/progression, six arenas, player movement, and night-arena WIPEOUT assignments.
- Keep courses fair and readable, with checkpoints and hazard coverage that increases through density and layout.
- Use `seedExtra` and `endlessLevel` for repeatable seeded obstacle variation.
- Bots should use grounded movement, jumps, stumble and obstacle responses, and fall recovery, while continuing after stumbles.
- Improve visual style and add differentiation to obstacles and enemy behavior.

## Decisions
- Qualifier, Sweeper, and Dizzy use tighter rival pacing and denser layouts.
- WIPEOUT remains dense but readable, with recovery-friendly checkpoints.
- Bot movement avoids duplicate vertical integration and uses course queries for grounding, gaps, and obstacles.
- Randomized selections shuffle each section’s obstacle pool using the course RNG.

## Work State
### Completed
- Expanded seeded randomized hazards across Qualifier, Sweeper, Dizzy, and WIPEOUT while retaining course sections and checkpoints.
- Reworked bot updates for course-ground queries, hazard and gap jumps, collision responses, grounded movement, and checkpoint fall recovery.
- Reset bot jump/collision state in `global.reset`.
- Confirmed `npm run build` and `git diff --check` pass.

### Active
- Improve graphics style, enemy AI movement/competition, and obstacle differentiation per the latest request.
- Add a course-generation test for same-seed determinism and different-seed variation.
- Review bot gameplay and course fairness/readability.
- Inspect generated `dist/` changes and decide whether to retain or revert them.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current implementation and identify high-impact visual, bot-competition, and obstacle-differentiation improvements.
2. Add and run a test proving obstacle type/order is deterministic for the same seed and varies across `seedExtra` values.
3. Review gameplay behavior, rerun checks, and inspect generated `dist/` changes.

## Relevant Files
- `src/course.js`: Seeded course generation, hazard builders, layouts, checkpoints, and ground queries.
- `src/bots.js`: Bot movement, grounding, collision response, and fall recovery.
- `src/game.js`: Course construction and seed inputs, including `seedExtra` and `endlessLevel`.
- `src/obstacles.js`: Obstacle rendering and behavior, relevant to differentiation.
- `src/characters.js`: Character presentation, relevant to graphics style.
- `src/style.css`: Game visual styling.
- `package.json`: Existing scripts; no course-generation test script currently defined.
- `dist/`: Generated output with existing and build-generated changes requiring review.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted across `src/characters.js`, `src/input.js`, `src/obstacles.js`, `src/player.js`, `src/style.css`, `capture.sh`, and `start.sh`; `vite.config.js` is untracked.
- `dist/` had pre-existing modifications/deletions and was further changed by the successful build, including `dist/assets/index-BqIsDU2E.js` and `dist/assets/index-D1it8Ek5.css`.
- Build emits a non-fatal warning that the JavaScript chunk is about 809 kB, above the 500 kB threshold.
